correctness.rationale: Direct proof: the cyclic group-ring cokernel gains the relations w^L=1 and a^h=1; Bezout gives w^g=c and Cartan sum B N_g(w)=0. The converse reconstructs z^n=1 and the Cartan relation. Since B(c-1)=0 in S, the principal ideal is the primitive-vector S-submodule B(1,...,1), giving S^(g-1) plus S/(B), exactly the stated SNF. All n>=1, L>=3, a>=1 and singular a=1 cases are included; 406 independent exact Smith computations and 1458 direct modular row reductions passed; finite checks are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed difference is a complete integral Smith-group and equivariant cokernel classification after positive-integer evaluation for the nonquadratic uniformly truncated cyclic Nakayama family. Bessenrodt–Holm 2005 Proposition 4.1 establishes unimodular normal forms for quadratic gentle algebras and is explicitly excluded as a novelty source. Zhao–Zhang 2020 already states the matching determinant in its accessible abstract, and that formula is credited. Telloni–Williams proves polynomial-field, not specialized integral, Smith forms. The 2018 Cartan-group work concerns other algebra classes. The 2017 and 2020 complete texts were inaccessible and are acknowledged as specific historical-priority risks; this is a provisional self-review, not independence or exhaustive uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: The Cartan group is a standard representation-theoretic integral invariant. Exact invariant factors and cyclic module action give full prime-primary torsion, finite-field rank-jump spectra and residual cyclic symmetry for all uniform cyclic Nakayama sizes and integral grading evaluations. The explicit g=gcd(n,L) transition unifies singular ordinary Cartan and finite weighted specializations; it is not a small arbitrary single-parameter table or a restatement of the already-known determinant.
